accessrestrict.head: Access Restrictions
accessrestrict.p: The bulk of the Franklin County (Va.) Free and Enslaved Records, 1837-1864, are digitized and available through Virginia Untold: The African American Narrative Digital Collection on the Library of Virginia website. Please use digital images where possible.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Franklin County (Va.) Free and Enslaved Records, 1837-1864. Local government records collection, Franklin County Court Records. The Library of Virginia, Richmond, Virginia.

acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: These records came to the Library of Virginia in a transfer of court papers from Franklin County (Va.) as part of an undated accession.

processinfo.head: Processing Information

p.emph: Starting in 2023, Library of Virginia archival staff in partnership with the Virginia Untold Project Manager began efforts to describe records related to free and enslaved Black and Multiracial people in a manner that improved the historical context of the records. In doing so, in some cases material once described within the "Free and Enslaved" record group for a locality may no longer be described within this record. When this has occurred, please see the Processing Information and Related Materials section for records that have been described separately.

processinfo.p: These records have been processed, indexed, and mostly scanned by G. Crawford, L. Neuroth, and LVA Staff for the purposes of digitizing them for the digital project Virginia Untold: The African American Narrative.
Apprenticeship Indentures were removed from this record in May 2026 and are now described in Franklin County (Va.) Apprenticeship Indentures, 1861.
"Free Negro" Registrations were removed from this record in June 2026 and are now described in Franklin County (Va.) Records related to the Registration of Free Persons, 1846-1851.
Encoded by S. Nerney: July 2009; updated by C. Collins: July 2026.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Free and Enslaved Records collection is comprised of miscellaneous records related to the regulation and policing of both enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people in Franklin County. The localities/local government authorities were largely responsible for enforcing laws that restricted the movement of enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people and the resulting documentation was often filed in the circuit courts. The ways in which local authorities enacted legal measures against or on behalf of enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people varied from locality to locality; therefore, records were not necessarily standardized or filed and retained in a consistent manner. This collection is topical and a means by which to compile miscellaneous documents related to free and enslaved people that are not established local government record types.
See: the Virginia Untold Record Types on the Library of Virginia website for additional context concerning "Free Negro" Tax Records and Requisitions for Public Use.

Locality History: Franklin County was named for Benjamin Franklin and was formed from Bedford and Henry Counties in 1785. The county court first met on 2 January 1786. Part of Patrick County was added in 1848. The county seat is Rocky Mount.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Franklin County (Va.) Free and Enslaved Records, 1837-1864, consist of "Free Negro" Tax Records, 1837-1838; Patrol Records, 1853-1862; and Requisitions for Public Use, 1863-1864.
"Free Negro" Tax Records, 1837-1838, consist of three lists of "free negroes" returned for tax purposes. To varying extents, the lists record each person's name, sex, age, residence, and occupation.

Patrol Records, 1853-1862, are comprised of patrol appointments, which name the patrollers appointed and detail their term of service and the area they were responsible for patrolling. Several appointments specify that the patrollers are to "act without compensation for their services."

Requisitions for Public Use, 1863-1864, consist of six appraisements or valuations of enslaved persons sent to work on Confederate fortifications. The appraisements list the name of the enslaver, as well as the name of the enslaved person and their valuation. These records also include an enrollment of free persons who were selected to serve as laborers for the Confederacy. The enrollment includes a list of male free persons in Franklin County and includes additional information such as occupation and number of family members.

Records related to Requisitions for Public Use, 1863-1864, include several documents that list the names of enslavers and the number of persons they enslaved who were employed by the Confederacy to do such jobs as stable work and "recruting [sic] Government animals." Additional records include an appraisement of enslaved persons, which lists their name, the name of their enslaver, and their estimated value; a letter discussing Oyler and Ferguson's hands and their service on Confederate fortifications; and several lists that record the name of enslavers and the number of persons they enslaved who were "enrolled" in service.
